title: Knockout Bracket Check
story: You run sign-ups for a table tennis knockout tournament. Each round, players pair off and losers go home, so the field halves. That only works cleanly with 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, … players; any other count means someone gets a free pass (a "bye") in some round.
The organiser can type any number, including mistakes like 0 or -4. Before printing a bracket, check whether the count needs no byes at all.
task: Write isFullBracket(players). Return true if players is a power of two (1, 2, 4, 8, …), else false.
0 and negatives return false. 1 returns true: one player is champion without playing. Try to answer without a loop.

examples.explanation: 16 → 8 → 4 → 2 → 1: every round halves evenly. In binary, 16 is 10000: a single 1 bit.
12 → 6 → 3, and 3 players cannot pair off. Being even is not enough. In binary, 12 is 1100: two 1 bits.
1 is 2 to the power 0. In binary it is just 1, a single 1 bit.

hints: Write 4, 8 and 16 in binary, then 6, 12 and 20. What do the first three share that the others do not?
A power of two has exactly one 1 bit. So: does players have exactly one bit set?
Write 8 and 7 in binary: 1000 and 0111. Then 12 and 11: 1100 and 1011. What does subtracting 1 do to the lowest 1 bit and the zeros below it? What does n & (n - 1) give in each case?
n & (n - 1) erases the lowest 1 bit of n. If that leaves 0, there was only one 1 bit. Check n > 0 first: 0 and negatives are never powers of two and can fool the bit test.
bruteForce: While the number is even, divide it by 2. If you end at exactly 1, it was a power of two. That is at most about 31 steps, so speed is not the problem.
The edges are. With 0, "while even, halve" loops forever, because 0 / 2 is still 0. Negatives need care too. The bit trick answers in one step, and the only edge to remember is n > 0.

js: * @param {number} players  may be zero or negative
* @return {boolean} true if players is a power of two

tests.note: 0 is not a power of two; a halving loop never ends
even but not a power of two: defeats an "is it even" check
round number, not a power of two
2^30, the largest power of two in range
largest value: all 31 low bits set
smallest value: one bit set in two's complement, but negative

py: # A power of two has exactly one 1 bit.
walkthrough: In binary, a power of two is a single 1 followed by zeros: 1, 10, 100, 1000. So check that a positive number has exactly one 1 bit.
Subtracting 1 turns the lowest 1 bit into 0 and every 0 below it into 1; higher bits stay the same. So n & (n - 1) is n with its lowest 1 bit removed.
• 16 = 10000, 15 = 01111. AND gives 00000: a power of two.
• 12 = 1100, 11 = 1011. AND gives 1000 (8, not 0): a second bit survived, so 12 is not.
• n = 0: 0 & -1 is 0, which would wrongly say yes. That is why n > 0 comes first.
solution.timeWhy: One comparison, one subtraction and one AND, whatever the number.
solution.takeaway: n & (n - 1) removes the lowest set bit. Use it to test "exactly one bit set", and repeat it in a loop to count set bits one at a time.
